newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Gunmen kill Shi'ite Moslem in Pakistani city.
newsitem.headline: Gunmen kill Shi'ite Moslem in Pakistani city.

text.p: Gunmen killed another Shi'ite Moslem in the Pakistani city of Lahore on Wednesday, the latest in a series of sectarian attacks, police said.
They said two unidentified men walked into the office of Qaiser Hussain, a manager in a rubber company, in the Garhi Shahu district at about 9.30 a.m. (0430 GMT) and shot him dead.
Hussain, a father of six, had been associated with a Shi'ite religious organisation, running an imambargah (prayer hall), and was a former member of the Lahore municipal corporation.
Pakistan has been shaken by a spate of sectarian killings, blamed on rival Sunni and Shi'ite militant groups, in the run-up to the Shi'ite mourning festival of Ashura on May 18.

Hussain was the third Shi'ite to be killed in Lahore in as many days. A Shi'ite doctor was shot dead on Tuesday and an elderly Shi'ite shopkeeper on Monday. A Sunni Moslem militant was also killed in the Punjab provincial capital on Monday.
Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif said on Tuesday his government would strive for peace between rival religious groups but would take stern action if they failed to resolve their differences.

"The present government will make sincere efforts to try to bring about rapprochement between the people fighting in the name of Islam," he said. "It is unfortunate that those people who recite Holy Koran and Hadith of the Holy Prophet (Mohammed) have pointed their Kalashnikovs against one another."
Sectarian violence has killed at least 65 people in Pakistan this year and more than 170 last year.
